incidents.summary: HSBC was penalised $1.9 billion for US money-laundering and sanctions violations, and the Federal Reserve terminated its related enforcement action in 2022.

sources.title: HSBC
sources.quote: In December 2012, HSBC was penalised $1.9 billion (US), the largest fine under the Bank Secrecy Act, for violating four U.S. laws designed to protect the U.S. financial system.

sources.title: HSBC
sources.quote: HSBC acknowledged that for years it had ignored warning signs that drug cartels in Mexico were using its branches to launder millions of dollars

sources.title: Fed ends decade-long enforcement action against HSBC
sources.quote: The U.S. Federal Reserve has terminated a decade-long enforcement action against HSBC Holdings PLC

incidents.summary: The US CFTC fined HSBC $275 million for participating in the Forex scandal.

sources.title: HSBC
sources.quote: The bank was fined US$275m by the US CFTC in 2014 for taking part in the Forex scandal.

incidents.summary: The FCA fined HSBC £63.9468 million for transaction-monitoring weaknesses lasting from March 2010 to March 2018, with remediation supervised by the regulator.

sources.title: FCA fines HSBC Bank plc £63.9 million for deficient transaction ...
sources.quote: The FCA has fined HSBC Bank plc (HSBC) £63,946,800 for failings in its anti-money laundering processes.

sources.title: FCA fines HSBC Bank plc £63.9 million for deficient transaction ...
sources.quote: However, the FCA found that three key parts of HSBC’s transaction monitoring systems showed serious weaknesses over a period of eight years from 31 March 2010 to 31 March 2018.

sources.title: FCA fines HSBC Bank plc £63.9 million for deficient transaction ...
sources.quote: HSBC has undertaken a large-scale remediation programme into its anti-money laundering processes, which was supervised by the FCA.

incidents.summary: HSBC agreed in 2019 to pay $336 million to settle Belgian allegations of tax fraud and money laundering involving clients’ offshore accounts.

sources.title: HSBC
sources.quote: In November 2014, HSBC was accused of tax fraud and money laundering by Belgian Prosecutors for helping hundreds of clients move money into offshore tax havens.

sources.title: HSBC
sources.quote: In August 2019, HSBC agreed to pay $336 million to settle the case.

incidents.summary: HSBC reached a court-approved settlement of about €300 million to end French criminal and civil dividend-tax proceedings without admitting guilt.

sources.title: HSBC Agrees to Pay €300 Million to End French Tax Dividend Probes - Bloomberg
sources.quote: HSBC Holdings Plc agreed to pay about €300 million ($350 million) to settle a twin criminal and civil case in France into its alleged role in a dividend-tax scandal that’s embroiled some of the biggest banks in the country.

sources.title: HSBC Agrees to Pay €300 Million to End French Tax Dividend Probes - Bloomberg
sources.quote: The Thursday settlement deal was outlined and later approved in court by Paris Judge Peimane Ghaleh-Marzban.

sources.title: HSBC Agrees to Pay €300 Million to End French Tax Dividend Probes - Bloomberg
sources.quote: The accord ends an investigation by the Parquet National Financier against HSBC without the bank making any admission of guilt.

incidents.summary: HSBC Australia admitted systemic scam-protection failures and was ordered to pay a $35 million penalty, while its remediation programme had paid around $21.5 million in compensation.

sources.title: Federal Court orders $35 million penalty against HSBC for scam ...
sources.quote: The Federal Court has ordered HSBC Bank Australia Limited (HSBC) to pay a $35 million penalty after the bank admitted to serious failures in protecting customers from scams.

sources.title: Federal Court orders $35 million penalty against HSBC for scam ...
sources.quote: Her Honour held that HSBC’s failures in respect of the ePayments code were widespread and systemic.

sources.title: Federal Court orders $35 million penalty against HSBC for scam ...
sources.quote: Following ASIC’s investigation, HSBC has established a large-scale remediation program that, to date, has paid around $21.5 million in compensation, with further payments to come before the end of July 2026.

incidents.summary: ActionAid and Profundo alleged that HSBC’s financing over three years contributed to climate disasters and supported projects associated with environmental and social harm.

sources.title: New report by ActionAid exposes devastating human cost of HSBC’s climate damage | ActionAid International
sources.quote: A damning new report from ActionAid and research group Profundo reveals that HSBC’s financing of fossil fuels and industrial agriculture over three years exposed the planet to a shocking 357 million tonnes of carbon emissions

sources.title: New report by ActionAid exposes devastating human cost of HSBC’s climate damage | ActionAid International
sources.quote: From water shortages in Bangladesh and deforestation in Brazil to the displacement and inadequate compensation of communities in Tanzania, HSBC-linked projects are hitting communities hard.

sources.title: New report by ActionAid exposes devastating human cost of HSBC’s climate damage | ActionAid International
sources.quote: Water sources, including a local river, have been contaminated, collapsing fish stocks and destroying farmland, according to community members.

incidents.summary: TBIJ alleged that HSBC counted financing supporting climate-damaging activities towards its sustainable-finance target.

sources.title: Mines, pipelines and oil rigs: what HSBC’s ‘sustainable… | TBIJ
sources.quote: All these companies’ operations have not only been facilitated by HSBC – which claims it is “helping to lead the transition to a more sustainable world” – but have benefited from deals that the bank has labelled sustainable finance.

sources.title: Mines, pipelines and oil rigs: what HSBC’s ‘sustainable… | TBIJ
sources.quote: However, the Bureau can reveal that billions of dollars being counted towards this target are in fact helping to fuel the climate crisis.

incidents.summary: TBIJ reported apparent breaches of HSBC’s coal phase-out pledge through financing arranged in 2023 and 2024, prompting investor criticism.

sources.title: HSBC breaks climate pledge with billion-dollar Glencore deal | TBIJ
sources.quote: Yet the Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ) has found that in May 2023 the bank helped raise $1bn for Glencore, which had been ramping up coal production for the previous two years.

sources.title: HSBC breaks pledge to phase out coal for second year running | TBIJ
sources.quote: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism (TBIJ) can reveal that the bank helped raise $2.4bn last year in deals that seem to violate its phase-out policy for coal, the world’s dirtiest fossil fuel.

sources.title: HSBC breaks pledge to phase out coal for second year running | TBIJ
sources.quote: HSBC came under fire from investors last month for doing the same in 2023.
